question:
Refer to the exhibit. The STP priority of N7K-1 and N7K-2 are the lowest in the network.
Which statement describes STP on the vPC?
context:
N7K-1
spanning-tree vlan 1-10 priority 8192

vpc domain 100
  role priority 100
  peer-keepalive destination 10.1.1.2 source 10.1.1.1
vrf default
  delay restore 60
  peer-switch
  auto-recovery
  ip arp synchronize

N7K-2
spanning-tree vlan 1-10 priority 8192

vpc domain 100
  role priority 200
  peer-keepalive destination 10.1.1.1 source 10.1.1.2
vrf default
  delay restore 60
  peer-switch
  auto-recovery
  ip arp synchronize
options: N7K-1 and N7K-2 appear as a single STP root.
N7K-1 appears as the STP root.
N7K-1 preempts N7K-2 as the STP root.
N7K-2 appears as the STP root.
explanation: Peer-switch - Enables the vPC switch pair to appear as a single STP root in the Layer 2 topology. Use the no form of the command to disable the peer switch vPC topology. If both switches do not have peer-switch enable, the question is not informing the bridge-ID (mac-address + priority) to see which switch would be the root anyway.
theory: The vPC "peer-switch" command makes the two physically distinct Nexus switches present themselves as one single STP root, both originating BPDUs with the same designated bridge ID on vPC ports. This avoids relying on a single elected root (which would force a suboptimal L2 path over the peer link) and speeds convergence during peer-link or role failures. Because both N7K-1 and N7K-2 have peer-switch configured and the lowest STP priority in the network, they appear to the rest of the topology as a single STP root rather than one of them individually winning the election. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC and Spanning Tree)
